title: Histograms with Unequal Class Widths
standard_text: Construct and interpret diagrams for grouped continuous data, including histograms with equal and unequal class intervals.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on histograms: frequency density, frequencies from bars, reading histograms with unequal class widths and estimating from them. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: On a histogram, the area of a bar shows the frequency.
body_html:
How it works

When the classes have different widths, the height of each bar is the frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. Then the area of a bar is the frequency: frequency = frequency density × class width.

To estimate how many are above a value inside a class, take the fraction of the class width that is above it.

Example

The class 10 < t ≤ 30 has frequency 24. Find the frequency density.

Width = 20

24 ÷ 20

Answer: 1.2

Example

A bar for 30 < t ≤ 35 has frequency density 4. Find the frequency.

Width = 5

4 × 5

Answer: 20

Common mistakes

  • Plotting frequency instead of frequency density.
  • Multiplying frequency by class width.
  • Reading the height of a bar as its frequency.

faq.a: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. It is the height of each bar on a histogram.

faq.q: How do you read a frequency from a histogram?
faq.a: Multiply the frequency density (the height) by the class width: the area of the bar is the frequency.
